title: Symmetric positive-definite linear systems with normalized energy error.

model.instance: The unknown real matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ is symmetric positive definite, with $\kappa(A)=\lambda_{\max}/\lambda_{\min}\le\kappa$. Inputs $b,x_0\in\mathbb R^d$ are public.
model.parameter_domain_description: Assume $d\ge1$, $\kappa\ge1$, and $\epsilon>0$. Additional theorem dimension and accuracy restrictions are recorded by region.
model.description_zh: The matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ is symmetric positive definite, with $d\ge1$ and spectral condition number $\lambda_{\max}(A)/\lambda_{\min}(A)\le\kappa$, where $\kappa\ge1$. No absolute spectral scale, sparsity, or preconditioner is promised.
description_paragraphs: The matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ is symmetric positive definite, $d\ge1$, and its spectral condition number is $\lambda_{\max}(A)/\lambda_{\min}(A)\le\kappa$, where $\kappa\ge1$. No absolute spectral scale, sparsity, or preconditioner is promised.

operations.order_convention: Native linear action of the specified matrix; no derivative order of an unregistered scalar function is implied.

feedback_quality.description: Exact real vector responses, with no observation noise or rounding.

operations.coupling: Every query accesses the same fixed matrix; repeated queries are allowed.

public_inputs: Public inputs are $d,\kappa,\epsilon,b,x_0$. Neither $A$ nor its eigenvectors are disclosed.
oracle.query_domain_description: Right products map R^d to R^d, with only the listed right-product channel available. A q-column block costs q calls. Entries, inverse actions, shifted solves, and matrix-function actions are not free additional feedback.
oracle.description_zh: Inputs $d,\kappa,\varepsilon,b,x_0$ are public, with $b,x_0\in\mathbb R^d$; $A$ is hidden. At any $v\in\mathbb R^d$, query the exact vector $Av$. All responses use the same fixed matrix; repeated calls are not independent samples. Entries, inverse actions, shifted solves, and the full matrix are not free interfaces.
description_paragraphs: Inputs $d,\kappa,\varepsilon,b,x_0$ are public, with $b,x_0\in\mathbb{R}^d$; $A$ is hidden. Any $v\in\mathbb{R}^d$ may be queried for exact $Av$. All responses use one fixed matrix; repetitions are not independent samples.

metric.normalization: Compare squared energy error directly with ε‖A‖_op‖x0 − x*‖₂². A zero initial error requires exact success. This is not error relative to the initial energy norm.
metric.finiteness_conditions: The specified dimension is finite, and the model and spectral assumptions hold.
metric.description_zh: The energy norm is $\|z\|_A^2=z^{\mathsf T}Az$. If $x_0\ne x^\star$, the base loss is $\ell(\widehat x)=\|\widehat x-x^\star\|_A^2/(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|x_0-x^\star\|_2^2)$ and must satisfy $\ell\le\varepsilon$. If $x_0=x^\star$, success requires $\widehat x=x^\star$. This is neither relative initial energy error nor relative residual.

applicability.metric_and_probability_mapping:
Fix the auxiliary parameters in the source Theorem E.2 at $\delta_0=\eta_0=1/2$. Its sufficient dimension condition is $d\ge C\kappa^{13}$, its residual threshold is $1/d$, and its required success probability is $5/6$. Choose the hard-instance initial point $x_0=0$. Let $e=\widehat x-x^\star$, $\beta=\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}$, and $\mu=\lambda_{\min}(A)$. Then
$$\|Ae\|_2^2\le\beta\|e\|_A^2\le\varepsilon\beta^2\|x^\star\|_2^2,\qquad \|b\|_2\ge\mu\|x^\star\|_2,$$
so the relative residual on success is at most $\kappa\sqrt\varepsilon$. The condition $\varepsilon\le\kappa^{-2}d^{-2}$ ensures the source residual threshold. Run a $2/3$-success algorithm independently three times, spend one additional $A\widehat x$ query per output, and select the smallest residual. At least one run succeeds with probability $1-(1/3)^3=26/27>5/6$. If the original budget is $N$, the source theorem excludes $3(N+1)<c\sqrt\kappa\log d$, giving $N\ge c'\sqrt\kappa\log d-O(1)$. On the strip $d^{-4}\le\varepsilon\le\kappa^{-2}d^{-2}$, we have $\log(1/\varepsilon)=\Theta(\log d)$, while $d\ge C\kappa^{13}$ ensures that the reconstruction branch does not change the order. Thus deterministic CG and the unrestricted randomized lower bound match up to constants in this strip; this does not establish optimality for every $(d,\kappa,\varepsilon)$.

proofs.title: Deterministic conjugate gradients with actual Av calls charged
proofs.body:
Let $x^\star=A^{-1}b$, $e_0=x_0-x^\star$, and $r_0=b-Ax_0$. One charged product forms $r_0$; if it is zero, return the exact solution $x_0$. Exact conjugate gradients minimizes the $A$-norm error over $x_0+\mathcal K_t(A,r_0)$. For every degree-$t$ polynomial $p$ with $p(0)=1$, this gives
$$\|x_t-x^\star\|_A\le\max_{\lambda\in\operatorname{spec}(A)}|p(\lambda)|\,\|e_0\|_A.$$
A scaled Chebyshev polynomial yields
$$\|x_t-x^\star\|_A^2\le4\left(\frac{\sqrt\kappa-1}{\sqrt\kappa+1}\right)^{2t}\|e_0\|_A^2\le4\left(\frac{\sqrt\kappa-1}{\sqrt\kappa+1}\right)^{2t}\|A\|_{\rm op}\|e_0\|_2^2.$$
Thus $t=O(\sqrt\kappa\log(4/\varepsilon))$ suffices in the nontrivial accuracy region. The initial residual call and the one product per CG iteration are included by increasing the universal constant in the registered ceiling. Actual spectral endpoints are used only to prove the polynomial bound; the algorithm uses the public condition-number bound and tolerance. This argument covers arbitrary public $x_0$, not only $x_0=0$. The Krylov minimum-error property is the cited primary ingredient; the normalization and resource accounting are explicit here.

Its sufficient dimension condition is $d\ge C\kappa^{13}$, its residual threshold is $1/d$, and its required success probability is $5/6$. Choose the hard-instance initial point $x_0=0$. Let $e=\widehat x-x^\star$, $\beta=\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}$, and $\mu=\lambda_{\min}(A)$. Then
$$\|Ae\|_2^2\le\beta\|e\|_A^2\le\varepsilon\beta^2\|x^\star\|_2^2,\qquad \|b\|_2\ge\mu\|x^\star\|_2,$$
so the relative residual on success is at most $\kappa\sqrt\varepsilon$. The condition $\varepsilon\le\kappa^{-2}d^{-2}$ ensures the source residual threshold. Run a $2/3$-success algorithm independently three times, spend one additional $A\widehat x$ query per output, and select the smallest residual. At least one run succeeds with probability $1-(1/3)^3=26/27>5/6$. If the original budget is $N$, the source theorem excludes $3(N+1)<c\sqrt\kappa\log d$, giving $N\ge c'\sqrt\kappa\log d-O(1)$. On the strip $d^{-4}\le\varepsilon\le\kappa^{-2}d^{-2}$, we have $\log(1/\varepsilon)=\Theta(\log d)$, while $d\ge C\kappa^{13}$ ensures that the reconstruction branch does not change the order. Thus deterministic CG and the unrestricted randomized lower bound match up to constants in this strip; this does not establish optimality for every $(d,\kappa,\varepsilon)$.
